newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy metalworkers' accord not close - union chief.
newsitem.headline: Italy metalworkers' accord not close - union chief.

text.p: A renewal of contracts for Italian engineers and metalworkers locked in a wage dispute with their employers is not close, the leader of the Italian engineering and metal union UILM said on Friday.
"At this point, the contract doesn't seem to me to be close," UILM leader Luigi Angeletti said.

"I'm not optimistic because the government is not doing anything to defend its proposal, and (employers' association) Confindustria is finding it easy to hold its line that it won't make inflationary agreements. Therefore, agreements won't be made," Angeletti said.

The Italian government said after a meeting earlier on Friday between Prime Minister Romano Prodi and leaders of the three main trade union confederations CGIL, CISL and UIL that it believed an end was in sight to the protracted pay dispute and summoned union and business chiefs for talks on Monday.
Angeletti said that "anything is possible" at the meeting called for Monday, including an escalation of the dispute.
"And a general strike, even if the federations are not convinced. Sooner or later, it's inevitable. It depends how Monday's meeting goes," he said.
Gianni Italia, leader of the second engineering and metal workers' union FIM, said "today's meeting is a negative event because it did not resolve a single problem."

The dispute, which involves some 1.7 million workers, centres on renewing wage contracts for the 1996-98 period after the previous contracts expired last June and the extent to which workers should be compensated for loss of purchasing power in the last contractual period.
The government suggested in December that management give workers an average 200,000 lire ($125) per month pay increase.

Unions, which had been seeking a 230,000 lire increase, accepted the proposals but the main industry group Federmeccanica has stuck to its original 139,000 lire offer, saying it will not accept a deal that fuels inflation.
